 Duterte’s lawyers struggling against ‘overwhelming’ evidence, prosecution says
 -->
 Staff Report 10 seconds ago 
 House prosecutors in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial acknowledged that her defense lawyers are skilled litigators but claimed they are struggling to counter evidence drawn largely from the vice president’s own financial disclosures and official records.
 Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong, spokesperson for the House prosecution panel, said Sunday that the difficulty confronting Duterte’s legal team was not a lack of competence but what he described as the strength of the evidence presented against their client.
 “Alam niyo po sa ating palagay magagaling naman po, individually, collectively ang kanilang mga abogado. Just to be fair, these are effectively litigators,” Adiong said.
[Translation: In our view, their lawyers are competent, both individually and collectively. To be fair, they are effective litigators.]
 However, Adiong argued that even experienced lawyers would struggle to defend a case when confronted with evidence he described as difficult to overcome.
 “Pero kasi at the end of the day, depende po yan sa kaso eh. Maski po gaano kagaling ang abogado pero mahina naman po talaga from the start ang kaso at insurmountable yung ebidensya na pinipresenta ng prosecution, mahirap po talagang i-refute yan o pabulaanan yung mga alegasyon,” he added.
[Translation: But at the end of the day, it depends on the case. No matter how good the lawyers are, if the defense’s case is weak from the beginning and the evidence presented by the prosecution is insurmountable, it is extremely difficult to refute or disprove the allegations.]
 Prosecution points to Duterte’s own financial records 
 Adiong said much of the prosecution’s evidence came from documents prepared, submitted or associated with Duterte and her family.
 These include her Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs), which he noted were prepared, notarized and sworn to by the vice president herself.
 He also cited bank records submitted by financial institutions, tax documents and business records involving Duterte and her family.
 According to Adiong, these documents support the prosecution’s allegations that Duterte failed to fully disclose her wealth in her SALNs and did not divest certain business interests.
 The prosecution spokesperson argued that the defense faces a particularly difficult task because the disputed financial information originated from records associated with its own client.
 He also claimed that some witnesses presented by the defense had failed to rebut the prosecution’s allegations and instead provided testimony that strengthened its case.
 The claims form part of the prosecution’s case concerning Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth.
 Allegations remain contested 
 The defense has disputed the allegations against Duterte, and the prosecution’s interpretation of the financial records remains subject to examination by the Senate impeachment court.
 Adiong’s statements represent the prosecution’s assessment of the proceedings, not a finding by the impeachment court that the allegations have been proven.
 The Senate has yet to issue its verdict in the impeachment trial.
